incoming_learnings: No review performed; no new learnings claimed.

review.review: The full terminal observation at log line 4962 explicitly identifies a sewer crab as the killer; accepted decision 1649 (line 4959) lowers HP from 1 to 0. Earlier, a concrete avoidable attrition defect occurs in doorway combat: decision 1456 successfully surprise-strikes a wraith, but decisions 1457–1466 (lines 4322–4345) repeatedly use ordinary melee against the next evasive wraith despite 4–5 staff charges. Repeated dodges and unchanged wraith counts accompany HP falling from 36 to 19. The early rule-preparation controller calls the established-hold selector before the dedicated wraith controller; its ordinary damage scoring overlooks evasion. A focused correction now prefers an already-admitted magic attack against a wraith in that established hold, while preserving the initial surprise attempt, existing fallback and safety checks. A reduced public-evidence fixture fails with two expected assertions on original source and passes all six tests after correction. All 1,970 Python tests pass, with four skipped. Local reconstructed preparation state matches the recorded selections at decisions 1456 and 1457 on original source; the candidate first differs at 1457, where investigation stops without subsequent simulated observations. This is not a full-run reconstruction or evidence that the later fly pressure, retreat failures or death would be prevented. Four potion colors remain unidentified before death; the subsequently revealed healing potion was not known emergency healing.
review.learnings: An established doorway limits approach lanes but does not remove wraith evasion after the first surprise strike. Preserve admitted magic priority there instead of comparing nominal melee damage alone. Do not treat post-death potion identities as resources the living bot knew how to use.

recommendations.summary: Preserve admitted magic priority against evasive wraiths after an established doorway surprise strike.
